name: Electrocaloric chip cooler
subtitle: a processor that pumps out its own heat

effects.effect: an electric field makes certain thin films heat up or cool down
a one-atom sheet of carbon carries electrons extremely fast and blocks every gas

effect: an electric field makes certain thin films heat up or cool down
how: Data centres now spend roughly a third of their electricity on moving heat away from chips, and the hottest spots on a chip, a few square millimetres across, set the speed limit for the whole machine. A film that cools whenever a voltage is applied is laid directly over those spots and switched in a cycle, pumping heat the handful of degrees up to a carbon sheet spreader, with no pumps, pipes or moving parts; cooling is applied where the heat is made rather than to the whole package.
obstacle: Each cycle moves only a few degrees' worth of heat, so hundreds of layers would be needed for the lift a real chip wants.
why: Cooling the hotspot itself beats refrigerating the whole room around it.
real: A flexible 30 um electrocaloric polymer refrigerator cooled an external electronic chip by 17.5 K (Nature 2024) and patents and liquid-metal simulations propose integration into the die stack, but no experimental electrocaloric film cooling an on-die hotspot was found; the demonstrated hotspot coolers are thermoelectric (15 C at ~1300 W/cm2).
